lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Aeacus — in Pluto's name — give me the full tour. Everything in Hades.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's a lot of ground to cover, Menippus. The highlights, I can manage. You already know Cerberus — you came in past him. The ferryman, the lake, Pyriphlegethon — you saw all that on the way in.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Yes, and I know you run the gate, and I've had my audience with the king and the Furies. What I want now is the people. The famous ones. The ones from the old days.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's Agamemnon. That's Achilles. Idomeneus just there. Odysseus. Ajax. Diomedes. The best of the Greeks, more or less.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Good gods, Homer. [pause] This is what your epic poems come down to — tossed on the ground, unrecognisable, shapeless. Dust. All of it just dust and an enormous amount of nonsense. 'Strengthless heads,' indeed — well, you got that right. [to Aeacus] And that one — who's that?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Cyrus. And that's Croesus beside him, Sardanapalus above, Midas above him, and Xerxes over there.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So Greece trembled before you, did it? [to Xerxes] You — you piece of work. Bridging the Hellespont. Sailing through mountains. [looks him up and down] Look at you now. [turns to Croesus] And Croesus. [shakes head] Aeacus, can I hit Sardanapalus? Just once. On the ear.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Please don't. His skull is rather fragile. It's on the womanish side.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Fine. I'll just spit on him then. He was a hermaphrodite in life; I don't see why death should change anything.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Would you like to see the philosophers as well?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Zeus, yes.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: First here — this is Pythagoras.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Good day to you, Euphorbus — or Apollo — or whatever name you're going by today.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: And to you, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: The golden thigh seems to have gone.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: It has, yes. But never mind that — what have you got in the bag? Anything to eat?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Beans, I'm afraid. So: not for you.
lines.note: Deadpan. He's not offering them, just observing the awkward fact.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Hand them over anyway. One revises one's views among the dead. I've learned that down here, beans and a father's skull are not, in fact, morally equivalent.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Moving on — Solon, son of Execestides. Thales over there. Pittacus beside them. The rest of the group. Seven in total, as you can count.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Those seven are the only ones here who look cheerful. [peers at someone nearby] But who is that one — covered in ash like a loaf buried in the embers, with all those blisters?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Empedocles. Half-roasted. He came to us via Etna.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: My dear bronze-footed friend — what possessed you to throw yourself into a volcano?

lines.speaker: Empedocles
lines.text: Melancholy, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. Vanity. Pretension. A truly spectacular quantity of hot air — that's what charcoaled you, sandals and all. You weren't entirely without talent, which makes it worse. And it didn't even work — you were found out immediately. You were dead, as it turned out. [pause] Where's Socrates, Aeacus?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Off somewhere with Nestor and Palamedes, talking at great length.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All the same, I'd like to see him.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Do you see the bald one?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They're all bald. You'll need to be more specific.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: The one with the snub nose.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Same problem. They all have snub noses.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: You're looking for me, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I am, Socrates.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: How are things in Athens?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Plenty of young men who say they're studying philosophy. The posture and the walk — if you could see it — absolutely first-rate philosophers. The look is flawless.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Yes, I saw quite a few of that type come through.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You'll have noticed the arrivals, I imagine. Aristippus came smelling of perfume. Plato himself came having thoroughly mastered the art of flattering Sicilian tyrants.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: And what do they think of me, up there?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're a fortunate man in that respect, Socrates. Everyone considers you a remarkable figure who knew everything. And — I feel I should be honest about this — knew nothing whatsoever.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: I told them the same thing myself. They thought I was being ironic.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And who are these around you?

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Charmides. Phaedrus. And Alcibiades, son of Clinias.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Good for you, Socrates. Still practicing your particular art, even here. Still not neglecting the beautiful.
lines.note: Warm, not snide. This is the affectionate joke — Menippus genuinely approves.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What else would I do with my time? Come, sit with us if you like.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, I'm going to go and set up next to Croesus and Sardanapalus. I have a feeling I'm going to be doing a great deal of laughing once I start listening to them wail.
lines.note: Easy, cheerful. He's genuinely looking forward to it.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: And I have to get back to the gate before some dead man slips past me. You can see the rest another time, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Go on then. This has been plenty. Thank you, Aeacus.
